page.layout: One page of running text in one column. In the right margin, beside the verse line, one marginal note ("Lectio 19. Octob."). Below the last text line: catchword and gathering signature at the foot.

main_text.p: nendum, Quòd Deus est merces magna seruorum suorum. Gen.12.

4. Falsorum fratrum apertę uellicationes, clandestinæ obtrectationes, & technæ, quas [illegible, ~9 letters] Satanæ suggerit. Sed meminerimus, consolationes Christi superabundare in fidelibus seruis, &c.

Iam si quis, primùm ea quæ nos monent, ut in sancta uocatione perseueremus: deinde contraria, ea uidelicet quæ ab illa nos abfterret, perpendat: animad-uertet, neminem eorum, qui de sua uocatione ad hoc genus studiorum certò persuasi sunt, sine scelere eam abijcere posse. Cætera, quæ addi poterant, pijs ueftris meditationibus relinquo.
main_text.head: VERSVS IIII.

p.i: At Iehouah excitauit uentum magnū in mare, fuitq; turbo magnus in mari, & nauis putauit conteri.

main_text.p: Huius uersus [παραφραστικῶς?] expositionē è Psalmo 107. initiò adducam: ac deinde Logicè eundē interpretari conabor. Dauidis hæc uerba sunt: Descendentes in mare nauibus, qui q; faciut opus in aquis multis, ipsi uident opera Iehouæ, & mi-

page.notes: The Greek word after "quas" is too worn to read; the illegible marker stands in its place. The Greek word before "expositionē" is a doubtful reading (marked [?]). The marginal note's printed form ("Lectio" over "19.Octob.") is partly worn. The verse-reference heading "VERSVS IIII." is set as level 3. The printed text has "uertet" and "faciut" as printed; "abfterret" is printed without a space. A small ornamental mark in the right margin beside "Huius" is not text and is left out.
